finding.claim: Unauthenticated KV read, write, and delete on the admin listener: any /api/kv/* request reaches dispatch_kv_request with no authn/authz, and the listener is bound to operator-configured admin_addr with no loopback check.
finding.sink: kv/mod.rs handle_set/handle_delete (169-190) mutate KvStoreRegistry; handle_get/handle_list (153-211) disclose all entries
finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on the route or in dispatch_kv_request. No loopback check on admin_addr. MAX_BODY_BYTES 1 MiB (kv/mod.rs:25,129) and escape_json_string (health/service.rs:36-54) are present but are not authorization. Deprecated add_kv_endpoint_to_pingora_server (kv/mod.rs:230-235) has the same gap. Exposure depends on operator admin_addr (praxis_core, unverified).

finding.claim: Runtime clamp of body mode lets a Stream downgrade bypass the baseline SizeLimit/StreamBuffer ceiling; the module docs claim the ceiling holds but no enforcement exists in this crate for Stream mode.
finding.source: Client request whose route has an operator-configured filter that switches body mode to Stream
finding.sink: Unbounded request body forwarding (request_body_filter.rs:85) and response body (response_body_filter.rs:70)

trace.note: clamp_body_mode_to_ceiling applied to runtime body mode
clamp only bounds StreamBuffer and SizeLimit
arm (m, None | Some(_)) => m returns Stream unchanged
match on ctx.request_body_mode; Stream arm at 85 has no size check
doc claims ABSOLUTE_MAX_BODY_BYTES enforced regardless of declarations; not true for Stream

finding.guards_checked: Clamp bounds StreamBuffer and SizeLimit only (mod.rs:189-197). ABSOLUTE_MAX_BODY_BYTES fallback applies only to StreamBuffer{None} (stream_buffer.rs:114, mod.rs:448). request_body_filter.rs:57-59 returns before accounting when no body filter needs the body. Byte counting inside praxis_filter execute_http_request_body is unverified; if it enforces limits this is only a doc mismatch.

finding.claim: For HTTP listeners the max_connections permit is acquired per request and released when the request context drops, so idle keep-alive connections are not counted and the limit caps in-flight requests rather than TCP connections.
finding.source: Any HTTP client opening many idle keep-alive connections

trace.note: early_request_filter acquires per-listener permit via try_acquire_owned
new_ctx creates a fresh context per request, so permit drops at request end
contrast: TCP path holds permit for the whole session

finding.guards_checked: Global limit connections.rs:37-46 has the same per-request scope. Nothing in this crate bounds open TCP connections. Assumes Pingora calls new_ctx per request (standard ProxyHttp contract, not verified here); any Pingora-level connection limit is unseen.
